title: Snapshotless Erasure Orchestrator for Console Usage Events
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce an orchestrator service that performs deterministic, snapshotless erasure of PII-containing console usage events across streaming and batch analytics stores. The orchestrator coordinates targeted deletions (by event id, user id, or retention window) without requiring costly global table snapshots, and emits verifiable attestations for audit. Goals: minimize storage/read amplification during erasure, provide strong audit trail, support legal-hold overrides, and make deletion idempotent and resumable across retries and cross-region replication.
acceptance_criteria: Erasure requests (by event_id or customer_id) produce an attestation record with request_id and digest within 30s for >=95% of requests
No full-table snapshots required for deletions; service uses index-driven lookup + tombstone propagation to all downstreams
Deleted rows are scrubbed or replaced with deterministic pseudonyms where downstreams require referential integrity (console dashboards)
End-to-end integration tests that simulate cross-region replication show no resurrected PII after eventual consistency windows
Audit export endpoint returns per-request proof (request_id, affected partitions, event counts) and matches observed deletion metrics in Console within 1 minute
implementation_notes: Workflow: accept deletion job -> build compact index query (time window + id filters) -> stream identifiers to deletion worker pool -> apply local tombstone marker + optional field-level redaction -> emit deletion-complete event to 'erasure-events' Kafka topic -> downstream consumers subscribe and apply tombstones to materialized views

Index selection: use existing partitioned event index (date + org_id) to avoid scan. For older cold partitions, trigger background compaction job to prune tombstones and enforce physical deletion according to policy.

Idempotency: workers persist request progress in a small dedicated KV store (request_id -> last_processed_key) to support resume and at-least-once semantics. Use monotonic per-partition cursors to avoid reprocessing large ranges.
Referential integrity: where dashboards reference event ids, substitute a stable pseudonym token derived from a per-tenant HMAC key so joins remain possible without exposing PII.
Backpressure: deletion throughput must be throttled by node IO and query SLOs. Implement token-bucket per-cluster and prioritize retention SLA-critical jobs.

Data stores: primary writes to event-store (ClickHouse) and streaming publish to 'erasure-events' topic. Additional adapters for BigQuery and internal analytics data lake will be implemented as consumers.
Testing: include chaos tests that kill worker nodes mid-job, simulate duplicate erasure events, and validate attestation consistency. Add conformance suite for third-party consumer adapters.
monitoring_and_rollout: Expose metrics: deletion_jobs_total, deletion_jobs_failed, deletion_latency_seconds{quantiles}, tombstones_emitted_total, attestation_generation_latency_seconds
SLOs: 99% of deletion jobs initiated succeed within 10 minutes for windows < 1M rows. Pager if deletion_job_failure_rate > 1% over 5m for Production orgs.

Phased rollout: Canary on staging with synthetic tenant -> opt-in beta for 5 customers (low-risk) -> gradual ramp to 25% of production traffic -> full rollout. Each phase gated by success metrics and security review acceptance.
Rollback: keep flag to switch workers to 'dry-run' emitting attestation but not applying tombstones. Also keep ability to replay erasure-events topic after rollback for reapplication.
Audits: monthly attestation export stored in KMS-encrypted bucket with retention aligned to legal policy; provide one-click auditor export in Console for customers with enterprise contracts.

Runbook: include steps for stuck jobs (inspect progress cursor, restart worker with --replay-from), and for suspected data resurrection (run scan job comparing attestation counts to current materialized view counts).

2025-02-13 - Diego Morales: Implemented request-level progress cursor and persisted it in the erasure_kv store. Working on optimistic concurrency for worker scaling.
